one_month_reasoning: The 1-month mark is the Fri Oct 30 close (Nov 1 is a Sunday). Avnet's fiscal Q1 FY27 ends Oct 3; since Feb 2023 every Q1-Q3 earnings 8-K has been filed exactly 32 days after quarter-end (supervisor's EDGAR check, consistent with my round-1 Nov 4-5 call), so the print is most likely Wed Nov 4, outside the window, with ~10% chance it lands by Oct 30. Arrow has also shifted later (~Nov 5), so its Q3 read-across is probably outside too. In-window drivers are TI and analog/MCU supplier Q3 reports (~Oct 20-28), SIA's August sales print (early Oct), ECIA sentiment and the October Fusion Greensheet (late Oct). Alt-data still shows tight analog/passives supply with selective spot cooling in mainstream DDR5/NAND; read-throughs lean mildly positive and momentum is positive, offset by pre-earnings de-risking with the stock at a 52-week high. I centre at ~$107.3 (about +0.3%) with ~10.5% monthly sigma (37%/3.5) and slightly fat tails; no earnings-gap widening.

fair_value.method: Blend of peak-cycle P/E (FY28E EPS $12.40 on ~86M diluted shares x 9x = ~$111.5, weight 55%) and EV/EBIT (FY27E EBIT ~$1.48B x 8x = EV $11.8B, less ~$3.5B forward net debt [reported $3.06B], over ~86M diluted shares = ~$97, weight 45%). Blended ~$105.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28E (NTM as of Oct-2027) adj EPS $12.40 x 9x peak-cycle multiple

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 guide $2.85 run-rated gives ~$11.40; modest sequential growth (WSTS sees 2027 market +27%, source 15) offset by thin, lagging consensus of ~$10.5 (sources 3; supervisor-checked 10.45-10.57) and pricing-normalisation risk.

~8% growth on FY27E as backlog extends into 1H27 (source 7), allocation persists into 2027 (source 4) and WSTS forecasts another ~27% 2027 market growth (source 15), but growth slows sharply and double-ordering risk rises (source 9); then ~1% trimmed for ~86M vs 85M diluted shares from the in-the-money convert (source 17).

Distributors de-rate to high-single-digit P/E on peak earnings (FY23 peak ~6x adjusted $8.06 per supervisor-checked data; 2000 allocation cycle, source 8, preceded a 2001 bust). 9x sits between the ~6x prior-peak trough multiple and the ~10x the stock pays on consensus today.

methods.name: EV/EBIT
methods.inputs: FY27E sales ~$37B x 4.0% adj op margin = EBIT ~$1.48B x 8x = EV $11.84B, less forward net debt ~$3.5B, / ~86M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 guide $9.15B midpoint x 4, roughly flat sequentially thereafter; matches the ~$37.06B consensus revenue.
Q4 FY26 adj op margin 3.8% (EC 4.1%, Farnell 9.0%); modest further operating leverage.
Cycle-peak discount for a low-margin distributor; consistent with ~9x P/E after interest and tax.

Reported: $734.0M short-term + $2,478.9M long-term debt = $3,212.8M less $155.4M cash = $3.06B. I use a forward ~$3.5B because FY26 operating cash flow was -$281M with receivables up ~$2.56B and Q1 sales guided up another ~10% sequentially; at reported net debt the leg would be ~$102.

82.07M basic (10-K cover, Aug 7, 2026) plus awards (Q4 diluted 84.69M, guide 85M) plus ~3.2M net shares from the $650M 1.75% convert at ~$70.27 with cash-settled principal at $107; no Q4 FY26 buybacks. Replaces my round-1 83M.

bear.story: Shortage peaks in 1H27; mainstream DDR5/NAND spot softening (Greensheet Sep-26) spreads, memory prices (now ~80% of the industry's 2026 dollar growth) roll over, double-ordered backlog unwinds, and by Oct-2027 the market prices falling FY28 EPS (~$9) at ~7x-7.5x on ~86M shares. Echoes 2000-01 for distributors.

base.story: Allocation persists through mid-2027 (WSTS sees 2027 market +27%), FY27 EPS ~$11.5, FY28 ~$12.4; multiple compresses to ~8.5-9x as investors look through the peak. Stock roughly flat.

bull.story: AI-led supercycle keeps book-to-bill >1 into 2028 (Arrow 'second inning'); EPS run-rate $14-15 and the market pays ~10-11x on a longer cycle; dilution from the convert partly offsets buybacks.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$70 the stock would be ~6x FY27E EPS of $11.5 (on ~86M diluted shares), the multiple Avnet traded at on its FY23 peak earnings. Reaching it inside 12 months would most likely mean the market sees shortage-driven earnings as peaked and rolling over (order cancellations, double-ordering unwind, memory/passives price declines) rather than ordinary volatility.

key_uncertainties: Timing of the cycle peak and how much double-ordering sits in backlog.

Memory price pass-through: industry growth is overwhelmingly memory-price driven (WSTS memory ~$230B to ~$804B in 2026), so a memory price reversal would hit the headline cycle even if Avnet's analog/MCU mix holds up.
Working-capital-driven cash burn and rising debt during the upcycle (reported net debt $3.06B, likely higher after Q1).
Convert dilution rising with the share price (~3.2M net shares at $107).
Small (~10%) chance the Q1 FY27 report falls inside the 1-month window.
reasoning: Round 2. Avnet is in a sharp components upcycle: Q4 FY26 sales $8.3B (+48% y/y), adj EPS $2.28, Q1 FY27 guide $2.80-2.90 (~$11.40 run-rate) versus thin FY27 consensus ~$10.5. Supervisor fixes I accept: diluted shares ~86M not 83M (82.07M basic plus awards plus ~3.2M net convert shares; no Q4 buybacks), which cuts my EV/EBIT leg to ~$97 and trims EPS ~1%; net debt is now labelled ($3.06B reported, ~$3.5B forward estimate I keep using for working-capital build). I checked the CEO sale on EDGAR: the Aug 12, 2026 Form 4 shows option exercises of 51,900 shares ($29-40 strikes) and same-day sale at $98.46, leaving directly held common unchanged at 168,923, followed by a 120,991-share award on Aug 20; my round-1 '24% of holdings' framing overstated it, so I drop it as a bearish signal (other officers' sales are small and tax/exercise related). On SIA's +135% y/y: WSTS data show memory going from ~$230B to ~$804B of a ~$796B to ~$1,511B market, so ~80% of the dollar growth is memory price/HBM and non-memory grows ~25%; the +135% print is a memory-price extreme, not a general volume peak, so I use it less as a cycle-top base rate for Avnet, but it heightens memory-reversal risk. WSTS also forecasts 2027 +27%, which supports earnings through most of my horizon. Net: fair value $105 (P/E $111.5 at 55%, EV/EBIT $97 at 45%); scenarios $66/$108/$150 at 25/50/25 (EV ~$108). The ladder is lognormal-like with median ~$105 and sigma ~0.40 (above 37% realized for cycle-turn risk), slightly fat left tail; moved down ~1 point in the middle from round 1. I keep my own 9x/8x multiples rather than the supervisor's $100 since my FY28 EPS view ($12.4) is above consensus on the guide run-rate. 1-month: earnings most likely Nov 4, outside the window, so ~10.5% sigma around ~$107.3. Research limits: X/Reddit not fetchable; WSTS figures come via trade press (bits-chips, anysilicon) not the WSTS release itself.
